description.value: The study examined event-related fMRI responses to smoking and control cues in dependent smokers following overnight abstinence and smoking as usual, and correlated abstinence-induced changes in craving with changes in hemodynamic response amplitude.

spans.text: Thus, the present study sought to assess event-related brain responses to smoking cues in dependent smokers following overnight abstinence and following smoking as usual (satiety).

description.value: The Shiffman/Jarvik Withdrawal Questionnaire is a 32-item, seven-point scale administered at the beginning and end of each scanning session to characterize nicotine withdrawal symptoms across craving, negative affect, arousal, appetite, habit withdrawal, and somatic symptoms. spans.text: The SWQ is a 32-item scale measuring nicotine withdrawal symptoms in the following dimensions: Craving (eg ‘Do you have an urge to smoke a cigarette?’), Negative Affect (eg ‘Do you feel tense?’), Arousal (eg ‘Do you feel wide awake?’), Appetite (eg ‘Do you feel hungrier than usual?’), Habit Withdrawal (eg ‘Do you miss having something to do with your hands?’), and Somatic Symptoms (eg ‘Is your heart being faster than usual?’).
